Every price in this report is the Friday 2026-11-06 close, refreshed at synthesis and re-confirmed identical (finnhub, asof 2026-11-06T21:00:00Z, market_session: closed). That is the freshest honest equity price available, not stale data. No idea here is actionable before the Monday 2026-11-09 open, and there is no same-day-tradeable idea at all — stated plainly rather than filled with a coin flip. Research set a crypto candidate aside deliberately: the instruments exist (IBIT, /MBT, spot) but BTC sits mid-range 5.8% below its own trend with no dated catalyst this week, and an honest 2.5-ATR crypto stop is 7.7% wide, needing a ~19% target above the 90-day high to clear the 2.0 swing floor.

WHY THE MIX LOOKS LIKE THIS. 9 ideas: 3 new (ACM, NVDA, RSP) and 6 position management — 2 exits and 4 stop amendments on filled positions. That is the honest output of a Saturday with a book of 11 open positions that needed decisions more than it needed additions, and the position management is not padding: per the phase contract, position updates are not new risk and do not count against the idea count. Read that way the new-idea count is 3. No per-horizon quota was applied and nothing was trimmed to a count; every candidate that cleared its floors is published.

THE TWO EXITS CARRY stop: null AND position_size_pct: 0 BY DESIGN. XLE and BCC are sell-to-close instructions on filled long positions, not new short ideas — direction 'sell' means close the position at the Monday open, and 'target' is set to Friday's close because that is where the exit happens. They have no stop because a position being closed at market does not need one. Do not read either as an invitation to short. XLE's old 60.80 stop now sits 0.45 ATR below the close, so it is noise rather than a thesis test; BCC's cyclical thesis is falsified by XHB +6.91% over the month BCC fell 5.36%, a 12.27-point shortfall against its own sector.

THE FOUR STOP AMENDMENTS WILL FAIL THE MECHANICAL STOP-DISTANCE CHECK, and that is a harness limitation on amendments rather than four tight stops. check_stop_distance measures the stop against the entry; on a filled position that has moved, the risk actually sits at the current price. Measured from Friday's close the distances clear their floors: KHC 2.22 ATR, ABT 2.03 ATR, PYPL 2.04 ATR, HII 2.02 ATR. Measured from the historical entry they read 0.13, 0.16, 0.37 and 0.16 ATR. The entries on these four are historical and must not be re-entered — a filled position can have its exits amended but never its entry. HII is the most material of the four: it is the best open gain in the book at +10.2% and carried no defined downside at all until this stop.

ALL THREE NEW IDEAS LAND AT EXACTLY 2.00 R:R, which is the signature worth being suspicious of, so here is the construction: on each one the stop was set first from the ATR floor and the target taken from what the 2.0 floor then implied, not the reverse. Only NVDA's target sits inside its existing range. Win probabilities (0.40, 0.40, 0.42) are 6.7-8.7 points over the 0.333 driftless baseline, a modest claim rather than a large one.

BCC's CONVICTION IS RECORDED AT 4 THOUGH ITS EVIDENCE MECHANICALLY SCORES 5 (four distinct kinds: positioning, primary_document, technical_level, counter_argument_answered). Marked down deliberately by research and left as found, because a conviction-5 label implies the 4-5% sizing tier for a position being closed at 0%. TRACK-RECORD CONTEXT THAT SHAPED TODAY'S BAR. 39 closed of 63 tracked: 4/39 hit target (10%), average -5.9%; stocks 1/26 (4%), ETFs 3/13 (23%), long_term 0/4 at -15.2%. n=39 is past the noise threshold, so research set an explicit bar — a new long equity swing idea must carry a dated catalyst inside the horizon or evidence beyond 'cheap and near support', because pullback-entry longs are the losing pattern. Both new stock ideas carry a dated earnings catalyst. The same record is why four of today's ideas protect open gains rather than reaching for targets.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, and what each cost:
- Event contracts: total loss, and the most valuable thing to fix. The events helper filters the first 200 unordered Kalshi markets, which are all sports parlays, so every macro search returns 0. Querying by series_ticker directly found the series live (KXCPIYOY, KXFED, KXBTC, KXRECSSNBER and others) but every price field — yes_bid, yes_ask, last_price, volume, open_interest, liquidity — is null without auth, on both the list and single-market endpoints. Zero event candidates, and the universe rule forbids stating an implied probability that could not be fetched. A tooling gap, not an absence of mispricing.
- Yahoo Finance chart API, HTTP 429 on every macro field: no VIX, no DXY, no index or futures quotes, no gold, no WTI. Those four appear as null in market_context.levels rather than estimated, and the equity regime had to be read off SPY/QQQ/IWM/RSP ETF closes.
- Yahoo options, HTTP 401: no options-implied move on any name, so no target was checked against a straddle. Target feasibility is argued from ATR multiples and prior swings only.
- Nasdaq short interest, ReadTimeout: no short interest or days-to-cover on any name.
- No economic-release calendar was reachable. That is why XHB sits on the watchlist with no dateable catalyst, and why the 2026-11-04/05 pivot across every rate-sensitive group (XHB, ROST, TJX, CEG all reversing on one day) is recorded as an observed pattern with no cause attributed to it.
- Nasdaq history for BTC-USD/ETH-USD returned no rows, and CoinGecko's free /ohlc gives ~4-day buckets for days=90, so no daily-resolution crypto ATR exists this run; daily crypto volatility was read off IBIT (3.09%) instead, whose -13.18% drawdown matches BTC's own -13.23%.
Sources that worked: finnhub (quotes, earnings calendar, insider transactions, analyst trend, quarterly actuals), nasdaq (daily OHLCV, ATR, SMA), FRED (rates, unemployment, CPI), CoinGecko (crypto spot), SEC EDGAR (filings).

recommendations.thesis: NVDA closed Friday at 186.64, just 2.85% above its 120-day low of 181.46, after falling 19.02% in a month against an SPY down 4.99% — so this is a sector unwind, not an index correction. But the multiple never justified one: trailing EPS from the four reported quarters is $7.01 (2.22+1.87+1.62+1.30), putting NVDA on 26.6x trailing and roughly 18.5x the annualised run-rate of the 2.5263 estimate, while EPS has compounded from 1.30 to an estimated 2.53 in four quarters, about 95% year over year. A business growing earnings at that rate on a high-20s trailing multiple at its 120-day low is the half of the semis selloff that is mispriced.
recommendations.key_risk: The 2.0:1 ratio exists only at 184.00 or better, and NVDA closed Friday at 186.64 after a +2.78% session — at the market the ratio is 1.62:1 and at the originally published 187.00 zone top it is 1.57:1, both under the floor. The entry is therefore a hard limit and the honest consequence is that this idea may never fill. The 2026-11-17 after-close print is a binary event inside the horizon and it is the dominant risk, not the de-rating — NVDA carries a 4.30% daily ATR and a disappointing datacenter number or any hint of order digestion can cover the whole 18-point stop in two sessions. A stop 9.8% below the entry does not protect against an earnings gap at all; it only bounds a drift lower. That is why this is sized at 3% and why the instruction is to trim half into the print. Conviction was lowered from 5 to 3 by the red team: of the four evidence kinds, positioning argues against the idea rather than for it — $1.38bn of insider selling with zero open-market buys, a 95.7% bullish and still-rising sell side with no estimate cuts taken, and a relative strength leg that amounts to falling 17.5% where the sector fell 21.5%. Three supporting kinds, not four.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that insiders sold $1,378,179,465 across 32 transactions in six months with zero open-market buys, and that the sell side is 95.7% bullish and still rising, so nobody has cut estimates yet and the Nov 17 print is where the cuts land — exactly the trap that makes AMAT untouchable. Two things answer it. First, the insider figure is routine at a $4.5 trillion market cap and is compensation-driven; the absence of buying is not evidence of a problem, whereas AMAT pairs the same selling with a multiple that only fell from 67.8x to 30.5x. Second, the estimate-cut risk is priced differently in the two names: AMAT needs its 30.5x trailing multiple defended on a cycle that may be rolling, while NVDA at 26.6x trailing needs only the growth already reported to persist for one more quarter. The de-rating from 34.7x at the 120-day high to 26.6x has already done the work the cuts would do. A third objection the original did not answer: the 220.00 target is the SMA50 at 219.81, which in a downtrend is overhead resistance rather than a magnet, and both moving averages sit above the price. The target being inside the existing 120-day range is still the strongest level argument in today's report — it is the only one of the three new ideas that did not need a new high — but it is resistance, and the trim-half instruction is where that is respected.

recommendations.key_risk: The 2.0:1 ratio exists only at 66.74 or better — Friday's close exactly — so the originally published 68.00 zone top shipped a 1.42:1 trade. The entry is now a hard limit at the close. The June 2026 quarter was a violent miss — actual -$0.50 against a $1.4809 estimate, a 133.76% negative surprise and a swing to a loss — so this is a company that has very recently blown up a quarter, and the 2026-11-16 print is a full-year guidance event that can do it again. The sell side has been trimming into the rally, with the bullish share down 6.8 points and the buy count falling from 11 to 9 since August. The target also requires a new high: 77.22 is 0.5% above the 120-day high of 76.85, so this pays only on a breakout, and the 5.51 ATR distance to it is the largest of any idea published today — on top of a stock that has already run 13.1% in 20 sessions, so part of the move the target needs has been taken. Positioning is the leg that found the idea and it is stale and wrong-footed: the three insider buys are dated 2026-05-14 and 2026-06-16, roughly five months old, all underwater by about 6%, and they immediately preceded the quarter that missed by 134% — insiders who bought and were wrong are not a confirmation. The valuation anchor rests on annualising the three clean quarters and discarding the loss quarter; on the four actually reported quarters the stock is 17.8x, not 11.8x. Two solid kinds remain, dated_catalyst and technical_level.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the insider buys are stale and underwater — dated 2026-05-14 and 2026-06-16 at $70.63, $71.12 and $71.02 against Friday close of 66.74 — so three officers bought right before the quarter that missed by 134%, which makes them look uninformed rather than prescient. CDNL, the top hit on the same screen, is the cautionary version: seven insiders bought in August and the stock is down 62% since. Two things separate ACM. First, the price has confirmed what the insiders did not: ACM is +12.24% over a month and back above both moving averages, where CDNL trades at 14.56 against an SMA50 of 25.08 and is 84.9% off its high. Second, the valuation is anchored on reported earnings rather than hope — 11.8x the three clean quarters annualised, with the 77.22 target equal to just 13.7x that same run-rate, so the target needs a modest multiple rather than a re-rating. One correction to the level framing: the 76.85 '120-day high' is a window artifact. ACM traded at 85.82 within the last 130 sessions, so the 77.22 target is a new 120-session high but not a new six-month high, and the ground between 77 and 86 is prior trading rather than blue sky. That cuts both ways — the breakout is less demanding than 'new high' implies, and the May breakdown shelf is also real overhead supply.
